chunks: Al-Bazanti narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr, who said:
I asked him about a woman placing shade over herself while she is in ihram, and he said: "Yes."
I said: "Then a man may place shade over himself while he is in ihram?" He said: "Yes, if he is afflicted with shaqīqah, and he should give charity of one mudd for each day."

key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman under discussion in the ruling of ihram
key_terms.بِمُدٍّ: with one mudd, a measured amount given as charity
key_terms.شَقِيقَةٌ: a severe head pain or migraine-like affliction
key_terms.لِكُلِّ يَوْمٍ: for each day that this concession is used
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: a man in the state of ihram
key_terms.مُحْرِمَةٌ: a woman in the state of ihram

ai.seo_question: Can a muhrim use shade while in ihram during hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning shading oneself while in ihram during hajj. It permits a woman to do so, and permits a man in a case of hardship from shaqīqah, with the obligation of giving charity of one mudd for each day.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2676 - Al-Bazanti narrated from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, who said:

I asked Imam (as) about a woman placing a shade over herself while she is in Ihram.
Imam (as) said: "Yes."

I asked: "What about a man placing a shade over himself while in Ihram?"
Imam (as) said: "Yes, if he is afflicted with severe pain (shaqiqah), and he should give charity of a mudd for each day."
